record.title: Kirby Problem 1.69
record.statement:
Let $L \subset (S^{3}, \xi_{std})$ be a transverse link with

$$
sl_{\Sigma}(L) = -\chi(\Sigma),
$$

for some Seifert surface $\Sigma$. Must $L$ be strongly quasipositive?
record.background:
Source: Kirby's Problems in Low-Dimensional Topology notes. Original problem number: KP-1.69.

Literature notes:
(1) The self-linking number of an oriented link transverse to the standard
contact structure $\xi_{std}$ on $S^{3}$ satisfies the well-known Bennequin bound
[Ben83, Etn05]:

$$
sl_{\Sigma}(L) \leq -\chi(\Sigma),
$$

where $\Sigma$ is any Seifert surface for $L$. This problem therefore attempts to
characterize when this bound is sharp.
(2) Strongly quasipositive links are those which possess a quasipositive Seifert
surface, constructed from parallel disks by attaching bands with positive
half-twists [Rud92]. Such a surface is properly isotopic to the intersection
of the 4-ball with a non-singular complex curve [Rud83]. It is known
that if a link is strongly quasipositive, or bounds a complex curve of
Euler characteristic equal to that of some Seifert surface for the link, then
the Bennequin bound is sharp (see [Shu07, Proposition 1.G] or [Hed10,
Proof of Theorem 1.5] for a proof).
(3) In light of the above remark, one can ask if sharpness of the Bennequin
bound implies $\Sigma$ is quasipositive.
If so, then it follows that that any
minimal genus Seifert surface for $L$ is quasipositive. This is because the
self-linking number depends only on the relative homology class of $\Sigma$,
hence the Bennequin bound will be sharp for any other minimal genus
Seifert surface $\Sigma'$.
(4) The question in this problem has an affirmative answer for fibered links
[Hed10], links represented by minimal-index braids with fractional Dehn
twist coefficient $> 1$ [IK19], 3-braids [IK19], positive knots [Rud99],
almost positive knots [FLL23], and knots whose canonical and Seifert
genus agree [FLL23]. Hedden and Tovstopyat-Nelip have announced an
affirmative answer for links with two dimensional top group of Heegaard
knot Floer homology.
(5) These notions generalize to arbitrary contact 3-manifolds, with the Ben-
nequin bound generalized by Eliashberg to tight contact 3-manifolds [Eli92]
and strong quasipositivity generalized via braids in open books [BEH $^{+}15$,
IK19, Hay21b]. Geometrically, the class of quasipositive Seifert surfaces
is the same as the class of ribbons of Legendrian graphs [BI09, Hay22].
One can therefore ask the following more general question: Suppose there
exists a transverse link $L \subset (Y, \xi)$ for which

$$
sl_{\xi,\Sigma}(Y, L) = -\chi(\Sigma),
$$

for some Seifert surface $\Sigma$. Is $\Sigma$ isotopic to the Legendrian ribbon of a
Legendrian graph $\Gamma \subset (Y, \xi)$? This generalized question has an affirmative
answer for overtwisted contact structures [BCV09].

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-17)

**Status:** open  
**Classification:** OPEN-TRIAGE

**Current literature assessment.** Strong quasipositivity implies sharp Bennequin inequality, but the converse remains open.

**Verified partial progress.**

- Complex-curve/strongly quasipositive links give sharpness.

**Full solution or refutation.**

No converse theorem or counterexample was verified.

**What remains.**

Decide whether sharpness for a Seifert surface forces strong quasipositivity.

**Sources checked.**

- K3: A New Problem List in Low-Dimensional Topology, Problem 1.69 (2026). (authoritative_secondary): https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/kirbylistrep.pdf
  Evidence used: Gives the forward implication and poses the converse.

**Review notes.** Open is source-backed.

This is a dated literature triage; an open classification is not proof that no later or unindexed result exists.
